name: memory-citation-v1-seed
description: Personalized memory citation cases for Week3 Task3C. The default ablation suite does not call an LLM; these labels support deterministic citation scoring once structured citations are available.

cases.userQuestion: Have I made this abba left-boundary mistake before?
cases.notes: Direct personalized memory question about an active sliding-window mistake.
limitations: Agent-drafted citation labels pending human review.

cases.userQuestion: When I use last_seen, what window-shrink mistake from my history should I watch for?
cases.notes: Pattern-history wording should still ground to the sliding-window fact and episode.
limitations: Only one sliding-window problem exists in v1.

cases.userQuestion: Do I have a useful complement lookup skill from previous Two Sum practice?
cases.notes: Should cite the repaired skill and avoid treating the superseded same-index reuse fact as current.
limitations: The current tag matcher may miss the hashmap_complement_lookup fact.

cases.userQuestion: Should my old same-index reuse in Two Sum still count as my current blocker?
cases.notes: The old episode can be cited as history, but the contradicted fact should not be cited as current memory.
limitations: This case tests stale citation suppression, not free-form answer quality.

cases.userQuestion: What binary-search invariant did I learn for insertion point?
cases.notes: Should cite the active first >= target skill, not resolved binary-search mistakes.
limitations: Repair episode retrieval was a known weak spot in Task3B.

cases.userQuestion: Have I previously returned left + 1 in Search Insert?
cases.notes: Resolved binary-search facts are neutral here only if framed as historical, not current.
limitations: The scorer validates citation IDs, not wording nuance.

cases.userQuestion: When did I ask about Python dict.get versus checking key membership?
cases.notes: This should expose the current API-confusion tag-match limitation if citations come only from focused retrieval.
limitations: The fact is current in manifest but hard to retrieve through problem-tag scoring.

cases.userQuestion: Do I prefer short hints with one concrete next step?
cases.notes: Preference L2 facts are diagnostic-only in v1; the chat episode is the expected citation.
limitations: L2 preference facts remain expectedRetrievable=false in the manifest.

cases.userQuestion: Have I shown a recurring recursion weakness before?
cases.notes: A grounded answer should say there is no seeded evidence instead of citing unrelated memory.
limitations: No-citation cases need human review so absence of evidence is not over-penalized.
V1 has 9 agent-drafted citation cases and is below a statistically powered personalized memory benchmark.
The default Task3C suite does not call an LLM, so free-text hallucinated memory rate is unscorable unless structured citations are provided.
Preference facts are present in the seed manifest but not expected L2 retrieval positives in v1.
